claim_1.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from 30 healthy young adults vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) at days 0, 7, 30, 180, and 750 after primary vaccination (day 0) showed that both vaccines induced robust serogroup A- and C-specific IgG responses, but MPSV4 produced greater and more durable polysaccharide-specific IgG than a single dose of MCV4 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Antibody responses induced by meningococcal vaccines
sources.quote: Both vaccines induced robust polysaccharide-specific IgG binding antibody responses against serogroups A and C, as measured by ELISA. These responses peaked at day 30 (MCV4) or day 180 (MPSV4) (Fig. 1a). The magnitude and duration of the polysaccharide-specific IgG response was greater with MPSV4 compared to a single dose of MCV4 (Fig. 1a).

claim_2.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from 30 healthy young adults vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) at days 0, 7, and 30 after primary vaccination (day 0) showed that both vaccines induced polysaccharide-specific IgG2, IgG1, and IgM responses compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Antibody responses induced by meningococcal vaccines
sources.quote: Both MPSV4 and MCV4 induced polysaccharide-specific IgG2 and IgG1 antibody responses (Fig. 1b), as well as specific IgM antibody titers, which continued to rise until at least day 30 (Fig. 1c).

claim_3.claim: Serum bactericidal assay (SBA) analysis of plasma from 30 healthy young adults vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) at days 0, 7, 30, 180, and 750 after primary vaccination (day 0) showed that both vaccines rapidly increased serum bactericidal activity by day 7, peaking at day 30 and remaining above baseline through day 750, with no difference between vaccine groups in maintaining protective titers two years after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Antibody responses induced by meningococcal vaccines
sources.quote: Both vaccines induced a rapid increase in serum bactericidal activity (SBA), which was detectable as early as day 7, peaked at day 30, began to decline by day 180, yet remained substantially above baseline at day 750 (Fig. 1d).

sources.section: Results - Antibody responses induced by meningococcal vaccines
sources.quote: An SBA titer of 1:8 or higher, a correlate of protective immunity 22, was maintained in the majority of MPSV4 and MCV4 vaccinees two years after inoculation, with no difference observed between the two vaccine groups (Fig. 1d).

claim_4.claim: Luminex analysis of plasma from 17 MCV4 vaccinees at days 0, 7, and 30 after primary vaccination (day 0) showed a strong anti-diphtheria toxoid IgG response at days 7 and 30 compared to baseline (day 0) and compared to MPSV4 vaccinees.

sources.section: Results - Antibody responses induced by meningococcal vaccines
sources.quote: MCV4, which contains the diphtheria toxoid (DT) protein as a conjugate, elicited a strong anti-DT IgG response at days 7 and 30, whereas MPSV4 containing polysaccharide alone did not (Fig. 1e).

claim_5.claim: FACS analysis of whole blood from 30 healthy young adults vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) at days 0, 3, 7, and 14 after primary vaccination (day 0) showed that antibody secreting cells peaked at day 7 after both vaccines, but the ASC response was lower after MPSV4 than after MCV4 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Antibody responses induced by meningococcal vaccines
sources.quote: The ASCs showed a peak at day 7 in both vaccines (Fig. 1f). Surprisingly, even though a greater polysaccharide-specific antibody response was induced by MPSV4 (Fig. 1a, d), the magnitude of the ASC response induced by MPSV4 was lower than that induced by MCV4 (Fig. 1f).

claim_6.claim: DNA microarray analysis of PBMCs from meningococcal vaccinees at days 0, 3, and 7 after primary vaccination (day 0) showed that MCV4 induced 1,150 differentially expressed genes at day 7 with an antibody-secreting-cell/XBP1-associated signature, whereas both vaccines showed only small transcriptional changes at day 3 and MPSV4 also showed few changes at day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Workflow to compare vaccine transcriptomic signatures
sources.quote: At day 7 post-vaccination, we identified 1,150 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in MCV4 vaccinees (Fig. 2a). These DEGs bear the hallmark of antibody secreting cells (ASC), which is consistent with the enhanced frequencies of these cells (Fig. 1f).

sources.section: Results - Workflow to compare vaccine transcriptomic signatures
sources.quote: However, only a small number of DEGs were identified at day 3 post-vaccination for both MPSV4 and MCV4, and at day 7 for MPSV4 (Fig. 2a).

claim_7.claim: DNA microarray analysis of vaccine blood transcriptomes across five vaccine studies, using differential expression comparison, showed that B cell genes including TNFRSF17 were upregulated at day 7 after MCV4 and TIV, whereas innate and interferon-response genes including OAS1, OAS2, STAT1, STAT2, and TRIM22 were upregulated at day 3 after live attenuated virus vaccines compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Comparative differential gene expression analysis
sources.quote: Several B cell genes were up-regulated at day 7 in MCV4 and TIV vaccinees (Fig. 3b), including TNFRSF17, a B cell differentiation gene that is predictive of antibody responses to the YF-17D and TIV vaccines 4, 6.

sources.section: Results - Comparative differential gene expression analysis
sources.quote: Genes associated with innate immunity and interferon responses, such as OAS1, OAS2, STAT1, STAT2 and TRIM22 were up-regulated at day 3 post-vaccination with live attenuated virus vaccines (Fig. 3b).

claim_8.claim: Luminex analysis of plasma cytokines from meningococcal vaccinees at days 0, 3, and 7 after primary vaccination (day 0) showed little cytokine change after either MPSV4 or MCV4 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Workflow to compare vaccine transcriptomic signatures
sources.quote: Consistent with this, analysis of plasma cytokines revealed little change induced by either vaccine (Supplementary Fig. 3).

claim_9.claim: DNA microarray analysis of blood transcriptomes from recipients of YF-17D, TIV, MPSV4, and MCV4, using blood transcription module analysis, showed three distinct day 3 programs associated with antibody responses: a primary viral response for YF-17D, a polysaccharide response shared by MPSV4 and MCV4 anti-polysaccharide responses, and a protein recall response shared by TIV and MCV4 anti-diphtheria toxoid responses compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: Yet to our surprise, the early BTM correlation profiles at day 3 displayed three distinctive patterns (Fig. 5a and Supplementary Fig. 11) that represent the protein recall response (shared by TIV and MCV4 anti-DT), the polysaccharide response (shared by MPSV4 and MCV4 anti-PS) and primary the viral response (YF-17D).

claim_10.claim: DNA microarray analysis of blood transcriptomes from YF-17D vaccinees, using blood transcription module analysis, showed that higher antibody responses at day 3 after primary vaccination (day 3) were associated with greater interferon-response and cell-adhesion module activity and with lower cell-division/PLK1-signaling module activity compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: In the primary viral response (Fig. 5a, b, Supplementary Fig. 12), higher antibody response is associated with greater activity in interferon response and cell adhesion modules.

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: Inversely correlated to the antibody response are a number of cell division modules, including PLK1 signaling events.

claim_11.claim: DNA microarray analysis of blood transcriptomes from MPSV4 and MCV4 vaccinees, using blood transcription module analysis, showed that stronger anti-polysaccharide antibody responses at day 3 after primary vaccination (day 3) were associated with antigen-presenting-cell activation, complement, and proinflammatory cytokine modules, including dendritic-cell markers CD83, HLA-DR, and HLA-DQ and inflammatory cytokines CCL20 and IL1B, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: The anti-polysaccharide response at day 3 (Fig. 5a, top; Supplementary Fig. 12) contains a number of modules associated with antigen presenting cells and their activation, as well as complement and proinflammatory cytokines (Fig. 5b).

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: Gene members of these modules include dendritic cell (DC) markers: CD83, HLA-DR and HLA-DQ (Supplementary Fig. 14), and inflammatory cytokines: CCL20 and IL1B (Supplementary Fig. 13).

claim_12.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of human myeloid dendritic cells and monocyte-derived dendritic cells stimulated in vitro with meningococcal vaccines showed that MPSV4 upregulated the co-stimulatory molecules CD80, CD83, HLA-DR, and CD86 and induced IL-6, TNF, and IL-12p40 secretion compared to unstimulated cells, whereas MCV4 did not induce robust dendritic-cell activation.

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: Up-regulation of co-stimulatory molecules and secretion of IL-6, TNF and IL-12p40 was detected in human DCs stimulated by MPSV4 (Fig. 6a).

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: However, despite there being a correlation of the DC surface signature module to anti-polysaccharide IgG (Supplementary Figure 14b), MCV4 did not induce robust activation of DCs in vitro (Fig. 6a & Supplementary Fig. 16).

claim_13.claim: ELISA analysis of cytokines from mouse splenic CD11c+ dendritic cells stimulated in vitro with MPSV4 showed that MPSV4-induced dendritic-cell activation depended on Myd88, Trif, Tlr4, and Asc compared to wild-type cells.

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: Using these cells from the appropriate knockout mice, we demonstrated that DC maturation induced by MPSV4 is dependent on Myd88, Trif and Tlr4, as well as inflammasome activation (Fig. 6b, Supplementary Fig. 16).

claim_14.claim: DNA microarray analysis of blood transcriptomes from TIV and MCV4 vaccinees, using blood transcription module analysis, showed that day 3 modules associated with protein recall responses featured monocyte and Toll-like receptor signaling, including TNFSF13B (BAFF), TNFSF13 (APRIL), and BCR signaling, and day 7 plasma and memory B cell modules were positively correlated with antibody responses compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: The modules whose activity on day 3 correlate with HAI titers (TIV) and the DT-specific antibody titers (MCV4) are likely be part of a transcriptomic program associated with protein recall responses (Fig. 5a, lower right; Supplementary Fig. 12). This program displays many monocyte features, especially of Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling.

sources.section: Results - Distinctive transcriptional programs in vaccine antibody responses
sources.quote: Linked to TLRs are TNFSF13B (also known as BAFF, M25) and TNFSF13 (also known as APRIL, M48) (Supplementary Fig. 12d, Supplementary Table 2). Together with BCR signaling, these modules indicate the downstream activation of B cells. Plasma and memory B cell modules at day 7 are indeed positively correlated with the antibody response in both vaccines (Supplementary Fig. 18).
